bandReport.notes: Items 1-26, contiguous, no gaps and no repeats. Item 1 is whole at the top of p01-c1 and item 26 is whole at the foot of p05-c2 (followed by '[ P.T.O.'), so neither band edge is cut. COLUMN CROPS: the automatic gutter split is correct on all five pages and no question text crosses it — every stem and its four options sit entirely within one column. Two footer-only artefacts of the split, verified against the whole-page images and affecting no question text: on p04 the centred folio '9' straddles the gutter and appears as a partial glyph at the right edge of c1 and again at the left edge of c2; the same happens on p05 with folio '11' (full at the right of c1, trailing '1' at the left of c2). WITHIN-PAGE SPILL: item 24's three statements end at the foot of p05-c1 and its 'Which of the statements given above are correct?' line plus all four options continue at the top of p05-c2 — transcribed as one whole item, and it is NOT a band-boundary spill. Faint Hindi show-through from the verso is visible on several column crops; it is bleed-through, not printed content, and has been ignored (these are the English-only pages). FIDELITY: item 26 Statement II is printed as 'Subtropical and temperate areas have less dry winds' and is transcribed verbatim as printed. Item 7's Statement III prints 'bond-holders' hyphenated across a line break; recorded as the unhyphenated 'bondholders' since it is line-wrap hyphenation, not a printed hyphen. Items 3 and 17 print genuine data grids and are rendered as GitHub pipe tables with the roman-numeral row labels kept as their own leading column, so that 'in how many of the above rows' and 'how many of the pairs given above' still have referents; the leading header cell is blank in both because it is blank in the booklet. Item 25's options are printed in the non-standard order I and III only / I and II only / I, II and III / II and III only and have NOT been reordered. No mathematical notation occurs anywhere in this band, so no LaTeX delimiters were needed. CLASSIFICATION: every subject, chapter and subtopic resolves to a listed catalog value, so no soft subtopic warnings are expected from this band. Two are judgement calls worth a second eye rather than warnings: item 3 (three Government organizations mapped to their parent ministries) has no natural catalog home and is filed under Governance, Laws, and Miscellaneous / Legal Provisions because each row turns on a named Act, though Bureaucracy is arguable; item 6 spans an international grouping (statement I), domestic resource endowment (II) and a 2023 MMDR amendment (III), and is filed under Geography / Mineral Resources as the closest single home, though Current Affairs and IR is arguable for statement I alone.
